title: Coherent formal modules with support proper over the base form Serre subcategories
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, $f:X\to S$ a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] (so $X$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]) and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. Each of the following full subcategories $\mathcal C$ of the abelian category $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian] is a Serre subcategory, i.e. contains $0$ and, for every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C'\to0$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$, $\mathcal B\in\mathcal C$ if and only if $\mathcal A\in\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal C'\in\mathcal C$: (1) $\mathit{Coh}_{\text{support proper over }S}(X,\mathcal I)$, the objects $(\mathcal F_n)$ with $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_1)$ proper over $S$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]; (2) the objects $(\mathcal F_n)$ for which there is a closed subscheme $Z\subseteq X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $Z\to S$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $\mathcal I_Z\mathcal F_n=0$ for all $n\ge1$, $\mathcal I_Z$ the ideal sheaf of $Z$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] (that is, $(\mathcal F_n)$ is supported on $Z$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (3)).

proof.text: Obtain Noetherianity of X and the nonempty abelian structure. For any abelian structure, identify its zero-morphism structure with the canonical full-subcategory one using subsingleton uniqueness; the private anyZero wrappers transport the level statements.

Prove stalkwise support containment for monomorphisms using module_stalk_exact, and for epimorphisms using local lifts of germ representatives. A short exact formal sequence is exact and epi at level one. Its first term is a quotient of a later kernel, whose support is contained in that of the later middle term and hence level one. Stalkwise exactness also puts the middle support in the union of the outer supports. Thus the middle support equals their union.

Each level-one module is coherent, hence quasi-coherent of finite type, so its support is closed. The level-one module of a zero formal object is zero under the evaluation functor; its stalks are zero and its support empty. The empty scheme gives properness of the empty closed subset. Closed subsets and finite unions preserve properness. Together with the support equality these give the short-exact iff criterion for the first property.

For a proper closed subscheme annihilating every middle level, apply the annihilator calculus to the later kernel inclusion and its epimorphism onto the first level, and to the middle-to-last level epimorphism. The same proper closed subscheme witnesses both outer properties. For extensions, ideals J and K annihilating the outer levels have product annihilating each middle level by exactness and the calculus. Construct W as the actual subscheme of J*K; its support is the union of the outer closed-subscheme supports, hence proper. The arbitrary-structure properness criterion proves W proper, and ker_subschemeι identifies its annihilator ideal with J*K. The zero system is annihilated by the ideal of the empty scheme since an ideal product embeds in the zero level module.

Build each IsSerreClass using the private short-exact iff criterion: monomorphisms sit in their cokernel sequences, epimorphisms in their kernel sequences, and the reverse implication gives extension closure. Zero membership supplies ContainsZero.

split_report.summary: Split along the proof of Stacks 0CYV (tags 0CYV, 087X, 02MP, 0CYN, 0CYR, 0CYM, 01QQ, 01IN, 00E0 checked against tags/tags). Seven steps: supports in a short exact sequence via stalks (Supp F_1 = Supp G_1 cup Supp H_1), closedness of supports, the empty set proper over S (closed immersion), proof of (1) by 0CYN/0CYR, annihilator calculus (sub, quotient, extension gives product ideal), proof of (2) for sub/quotients and for extensions via the closed subscheme cut out by I_Z I_Y and 0CYL. Three new nodes: lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-short-exact-levels (Stacks' remarks (a), (b), which the abelian node does not state: its statement gives termwise cokernels only, kernels are not termwise), lem-weil-pbc-formal-system-support-constant (Supp F_n = Supp F_1, stated without proof by Stacks), both unsplit; lem-weil-pbc-product-ideal-closed-subscheme-union, a Mathlib leaf (IdealSheafData.support_mul with subschemeι, ker_subschemeι, range_subschemeι, Hom.support_ker). Statement unchanged in content; citations [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (for 'so X is Noetherian') and [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] (for I_Z) added, with stmt_deps.

lean.statement: theorem formalSystems_properSupport_serre {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (I : X.IdealSheafData) : Nonempty (Abelian (@CoherentFormalModule X (isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType f) I)) ∧ ∀ [Ab : Abelian (@CoherentFormalModule X (isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType f) I)], ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass (fun M : @CoherentFormalModule X (isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType f) I ↦ Scheme.Modules.HasSupportProperOver f (M.obj.obj (op 0))) ∧ ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass (fun M : @CoherentFormalModule X (isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType f) I ↦ ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) (_ : IsClosedImmersion i), IsProper (i ≫ f) ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct i.ker.toModulesι (M.obj.obj (op n))))
